items.note: DELETE /jobs/<id>, cancel and delete buttons, episode progress and an optional memory cap. The memory cap counts resident memory: the worker reads the job's process tree every 0.5 s and kills it past ARRIVAL_MAX_JOB_MB with a MemoryLimitError naming the stage (#192). The old RLIMIT_AS cap followed the core count and crashed jobs (docs/ref/MEMCAP.md).

items.title: Real GR00T loader check and fine-tune on hero_kitchen_sim
items.note: GR00T N1.7-3B fine-tuned on one 96 GB GPU and scored in the sim on identical trials. Best 39 of 48 (81%) against 26 of 48 for the clean-data baseline (paired sign test p = 0.007): clean data plus DART demos with the marginal drawer pulls removed. Self-reported in #165 and #63; small samples, and the base-GR00T and generic-RoboCasa cells (G3, G4) are not run, so `usefulness` stays null. Weights: https://huggingface.co/Ish1105/arrival-gr00t-n17-run4 (NVIDIA Open Model License, not the repo's Apache 2.0). The same card reports clean plus unfiltered DART at 22 of 48. The fine-tunes ran on one 96 GB GPU on Cosmos, not on Nebius.

items.title: Real GR00T policy server: chunking, both camera keys, golden-file test
items.note: Ran against real GR00T on Oct 21 (Isaac-GR00T dac54b3, N1.7-3B, one 96 GB GPU): /act returns 16-step action chunks for a request with both camera keys, and eval --policy vla scored the fine-tunes through it (docs/ref/POL-3.md). The wire-format golden test and the 8-float and 11-float schemas are done.

items.title: Prove layout.yaml loads in real RoboCasa
items.note: Built in real RoboCasa 1.0.1 (Oct 27): layout.yaml as written loads but RoboCasa reads its walls, floor, fronts and sink differently; arrival.twin.robocasa_layout converts it, and the hero kitchen and RoomPlan kitchen_real_01 then build with every fixture centre within 2.5 cm horizontally and no added overlap (scripts/check_robocasa_layout.py, docs/results/robocasa-layout-2026-10-27). The sink height is RoboCasa's (flush with the counter top).

items.title: Real MimicGen retargeting for counter_to_sink
items.note: Native object-centric SE(3) retargeting of counter_to_sink landed in #356 (arrival/generate/se3_retarget.py, physics-checked). Issue #62's benchmark ran on Oct 27: 14 of the 20 P3 teleop demos became seeds (retarget --teleop), and 140 attempts gave 104 physics-checked episodes that validate with 0 flagged, at 15.2 s each against 61.5 operator seconds per teleop demo (docs/results/g7-teleop-seeds-2026-10-27). Upstream MimicGen is still not integrated (arrival/generate/mimicgen.py only probes for RoboCasa).

items.title: One real Nemotron call on Token Factory, kept as evidence
items.note: Live on Oct 26: Nemotron Super plans (about 2.6 s each) and Lightning writes wordings through Token Factory. On 15 indirect requests the Nemotron planner picks the right task 13 times against 6 for the keyword parser, and on 54 Lightning-written wordings 52 against 47 (docs/results/planner-benchmark-2026-10-26.json). Evidence: docs/results/live-apis-2026-10-26.json.

items.title: One real Tavily call, for the Best Use of Tavily bonus
items.note: Live on Oct 26: queries rewritten against the live API so they return figures (e.g. the fridge's federal 66.7 N opening-force limit, citing ecfr.gov), at the advanced depth. The safety guidelines beside them are still our built-in table, labelled built_in_table.

items.title: Nebius Serverless Jobs fan-out with resume, then one real small run
items.note: Fan-out with done-markers, retry and resume is built. arrival fanout --backend nebius runs shards as Serverless AI Jobs with an Object Storage bucket, tested only against in-process fakes of both APIs. It has never run against Nebius. The hackathon rules count a project as running on Nebius only if it calls the Token Factory inference API or runs on Nebius AI Cloud (Serverless Jobs, Serverless Endpoints, or DevPods). Neither has been done. Not pursued for this submission: C6 meets the rule.

items.title: Measured time and cost per demo against the teleop baseline
items.note: Added arrival cost CLI subcommand with automated P3 teleop baseline comparison. Time is measured: retargeted counter_to_sink demos from P3's own seeds take 15.2 s of one CPU core each against 61.5 operator seconds, a 4.04 ratio from arrival cost (docs/results/g7-teleop-seeds-2026-10-27). Cloud dollar cost per demo remains to be measured with real usage.

items.title: Detect small objects from posed frames with a VLM
items.note: Live on Oct 26: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on Token Factory read the six rendered fixture frames, boxed the mug in all three mug frames and nothing in the empty ones; the mug was placed 1.2 cm from its true centre (docs/results/live-detect-2026-10-26.json). Rendered frames, not a real scan: real RGB-D frames wait on P1.

items.title: Real Cosmos variation on a tenth of validated frames
items.note: The restyle stage and its Cosmos client landed in #93 (arrival/render/variation.py, SIM-7a): about 10% of frames, edge and mask checks, honest labels. On Oct 27 NVIDIA Cosmos Transfer2.5-2B (edge control) ran for real on one RTX PRO 6000 and restyled three 93-frame sim episodes (open_fridge, counter_to_sink, open_drawer) into photoreal kitchens; all 279 frames passed the stage's edge check (correlation 0.74 to 0.83, threshold 0.6) and NVIDIA's guardrail (docs/results/cosmos-transfer-2026-10-27/). Still open: the dataset run, which calls the model through the HTTP client on a tenth of each dataset's frames.

groups.title: Devpost form
groups.blurb: Nebius x NVIDIA Global AI Hackathon, https://nebiusglobalaihackathon.devpost.com/. Deadline Friday, October 30, 2026, 10:00am Pacific. Physical AI is the track: a demo URL is not required, and with no robot the video needs at least one minute of the key modules (P4).

items.title: Fill the Devpost form: Physical AI, description, public repo, and feedback
items.note: Required on the form: the track, a text description of what it is, why, and how it works, a public GitHub URL whose About section shows the Apache 2.0 license, a README with setup instructions, the YouTube link (P4), and written feedback on Token Factory, AI Cloud, and the NVIDIA models used. Highlight GR00T and any Nemotron or Token Factory use. English. A demo URL is optional on this track (C2). If the project existed before August 26, 2026, say what changed during the submission period. The project has to run as the video and the text describe, and the rules require a real Token Factory call or a Nebius AI Cloud run (C1).
